sanskrit: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tathaiva sa munis tadā bharataṃ kaikayī putram ātithyena nyamantrayat
english: And that sage, knowing that Bharata had resolved to stay, thereupon invited Bharata, the son of Kaikeyī, with hospitable rites.

sanskrit: abravīd bharatas tv enaṃ nanv idaṃ bhavatā kṛtam pādyam arghyaṃ tathātithyaṃ vane yad ūpapadyate
english: But Bharata said to him: "Has not this already been done by you — the water for washing feet, the guest-offering, and such hospitality as is fitting in the forest?"

sanskrit: athovāca bharadvājo bharataṃ prahasann iva jāne tvāṃ prīti saṃyuktaṃ tuṣyes tvaṃ yena kena cit
english: Then Bharadvāja replied to Bharata with something of a smile: "I know that you are full of affection and would be pleased with whatever little is offered.

sanskrit: senāyās tu tavaitasyāḥ kartum icchāmi bhojanam mama pritir yathā rūpā tvam arho manujarṣabha
english: But I wish to provide a meal for this army of yours, as befitting my affection — you are worthy of it, O bull among men.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ cāpi nikṣipya dūre balam ihāgataḥ kasmān nehopayāto 'si sabalaḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: And why have you come here having left the army behind at a distance? Why did you not come with the full force, O bull among men?"

sanskrit: bharataḥ pratyuvācedaṃ prāñjalis taṃ tapodhanam sasainyo nopayāto 'smi bhagavan bhagavad bhayāt
english: Bharata replied with joined palms to that ascetic endowed with tapas: "I did not come with the army, revered sir, out of reverence for your sacred presence.

sanskrit: vāji mukhyā manuṣyāś ca mattāś ca vara vāraṇāḥ pracchādya mahatīṃ bhūmiṃ bhagavann anuyānti mām
english: The choicest horses, men, and mighty intoxicated elephants, covering the great earth, follow me, revered sir.

sanskrit: te vṛkṣān udakaṃ bhūmim āśrameṣūṭajāṃs tathā na hiṃsyur iti tenāham eka evāgatas tataḥ
english: That they might not harm the trees, the water, the ground, the hermitages, or the leaf-huts — for that reason I came alone."

sanskrit: ānīyatām itaḥ senety ājñaptaḥ paramarṣiṇā tathā tu cakre bharataḥ senāyāḥ samupāgamam
english: Ordered by the great seer, "Let the army be brought here," Bharata caused the army to advance accordingly.

sanskrit: agniśālāṃ praviśyātha pītvāpaḥ parimṛjya ca ātithyasya kriyāhetor viśvakarmāṇam āhvayat
english: Then, having entered the fire-hall, sipped water, and dried himself, for the purpose of performing the rites of hospitality, he invoked Viśvakarman.

sanskrit: āhvaye viśvakarmāṇam ahaṃ tvaṣṭāram eva ca ātithyaṃ kartum icchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām
english: "I invoke Viśvakarman and also Tvaṣṭṛ — I wish to perform the hospitality; let all be arranged for me therein.

sanskrit: prāk srotasaś ca yā nadyaḥ pratyak srotasa eva ca pṛthivyām antarikṣe ca samāyāntv adya sarvaśaḥ
english: Let all the rivers that flow eastward and those that flow westward, on the earth and in the sky, come together here today from every direction.

sanskrit: anyāḥ sravantu maireyaṃ surām anyāḥ suniṣṭhitām aparāś codakaṃ śītam ikṣukāṇḍarasopamam
english: Let some flow with maireya wine, others with well-brewed surā, and yet others with cool water resembling sugarcane juice.

sanskrit: āhvaye devagandharvān viśvāvasuhahāhuhūn tathaivāpsaraso devīr gandharvīś cāpi sarvaśaḥ
english: I invoke the divine gandharvas — Viśvāvasu, Hāhā, and Hūhū — and likewise the apsaras goddesses and all the gandharvī women.

sanskrit: ghṛtācīm atha viśvācīṃ miśrakeśīm alambusām śakraṃ yāś copatiṣṭhanti brahmāṇaṃ yāś ca bhāminīḥ sarvās tumburuṇā sārdham āhvaye saparicchadāḥ
english: Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Miśrakeśī, Alambusā — those radiant ones who attend upon Śakra, and those who attend upon Brahmā — I invoke all of them together with Tumburu, along with their retinues.

sanskrit: vanaṃ kuruṣu yad divyaṃ vāso bhūṣaṇapatravat divyanārīphalaṃ śaśvat tat kauberam ihaiva tu
english: That divine forest among the Kurus, adorned like garments and ornaments with leaves, yielding ever-lasting divine fruits for its women — that forest belonging to Kubera — let it be here.

sanskrit: iha me bhagavān somo vidhattām annam uttamam bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca coṣyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu
english: Let the blessed Soma ordain for me here the finest food — foods to be chewed, foods to be eaten, to be sucked, and to be licked, in great variety.

sanskrit: vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni pādapapracyutāni ca surādīni ca peyāni māṃsāni vividhāni ca
english: And varied garlands freshly fallen from the trees, wines and other drinks, and meats of many kinds."

sanskrit: evaṃ samādhinā yuktas tejasāpratimena ca śikṣāsvarasamāyuktaṃ tapasā cābravīn muniḥ
english: Thus composed in meditation and possessed of unequalled splendour, that sage, empowered by his asceticism, spoke with a voice modulated in pitch and intonation.

sanskrit: manasā dhyāyatas tasya prāṅmukhasya kṛtāñjaleḥ ājagmus tāni sarvāṇi daivatāni pṛthakpṛthak
english: As he meditated with his mind, facing east with joined palms, all those deities came separately, one by one.

sanskrit: malayaṃ durduraṃ caiva tataḥ svedanudo 'nilaḥ upaspṛśya vavau yuktyā supriyātmā sukhaḥ śivaḥ
english: Then a wind, touching the Malaya and Dardura mountains, blew fitly — cooling, pleasant to the soul, gentle and auspicious, dispelling heat.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyavartanta ghanā divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ devadundubhighoṣaś ca dikṣu sarvāsu śuśruve
english: Then divine showers of flowers descended from the clouds, and the sound of the celestial kettle-drums was heard in all directions.

sanskrit: pravavuś cottamā vātā nanṛtuś cāpsarogaṇāḥ prajagur devagandharvā vīṇā pramumucuḥ svarān
english: Excellent breezes blew; the hosts of apsarases danced; the divine gandharvas sang; the vīṇās gave forth their notes.

sanskrit: sa śabdo dyāṃ ca bhūmiṃ ca prāṇināṃ śravaṇāni ca viveśoccāritaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ samo layaguṇānvitaḥ
english: That sound, uttered and refined, even and possessed of perfect rhythm, entered heaven, earth, and the ears of all living beings.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde divye śrotrasukhe nṛṇām dadarśa bhārataṃ sainyaṃ vidhānaṃ viśvakarmaṇaḥ
english: When that divine sound, delightful to the ears of men, had ceased, the army of Bharata beheld the arrangement made by Viśvakarman.

sanskrit: babhūva hi samā bhūmiḥ samantāt pañcayojanam śādvalair bahubhiś channā nīlavaidūryasaṃnibhaiḥ
english: The ground became level for five yojanas in every direction, covered with dense meadows of grass resembling blue vaidūrya gems.

sanskrit: tasmin bilvāḥ kapitthāś ca panasā bījapūrakāḥ āmalakyo babhūvuś ca cūtāś ca phalabhūṣaṇāḥ
english: In that place grew bilva, kapittha, jackfruit, bījapūraka, āmalakī, and mango trees, adorned with fruits.

sanskrit: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaś ca vanaṃ divyopabhogavat ājagāma nadī divyā tīrajair bahubhir vṛtā
english: And from the northern Kurus came a forest yielding divine enjoyments, along with a divine river surrounded by many trees along its banks.

sanskrit: catuḥśālāni śubhrāni śālāś ca gajavājinām harmyaprāsādasaṃghātās toraṇāni śubhāni ca
english: Bright buildings with four halls, stables for elephants and horses, clusters of mansions and palaces, and beautiful gateways appeared.

sanskrit: sitameghanibhaṃ cāpi rājaveśma sutoraṇam śuklamālyakṛtākāraṃ divyagandhasamukṣitam
english: A royal palace resembling a white cloud, with a beautiful gateway, decorated with white garlands, and sprinkled with divine fragrances appeared.

sanskrit: caturasram asaṃbādhaṃ śayanāsanayānavat divyaiḥ sarvarasair yuktaṃ divyabhojanavastravat
english: It was square and spacious, furnished with couches, seats, and vehicles, stocked with all divine flavours, with divine food and garments.

sanskrit: upakalpita sarvānnaṃ dhautanirmalabhājanam kḷptasarvāsanaṃ śrīmat svāstīrṇaśayanottamam
english: All foods were prepared therein; the vessels were washed and spotless; all seats were arranged; it was splendid, with excellent beds well spread.

sanskrit: praviveśa mahābāhur anujñāto maharṣiṇā veśma tad ratnasaṃpūrṇaṃ bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ
english: The mighty-armed Bharata, son of Kaikeyī, permitted by the great seer, entered that mansion filled with jewels.

sanskrit: anujagmuś ca taṃ sarve mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ babhūvuś ca mudā yuktā taṃ dṛṣṭvā veśma saṃvidhim
english: All the ministers and the priest followed him, and they were filled with joy on seeing the arrangement of that palace.

sanskrit: tatra rājāsanaṃ divyaṃ vyajanaṃ chatram eva ca bharato mantribhiḥ sārdham abhyavartata rājavat
english: There Bharata, together with his ministers, approached the divine royal throne, the fan, and the royal parasol, in the manner of a king.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ pūjayām āsa rāmāyābhipraṇamya ca vālavyajanam ādāya nyaṣīdat sacivāsane
english: He honoured the throne, bowing to it in the name of Rāma, and then, taking up the yak-tail fan, sat on a minister's seat.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyān niṣeduś ca sarve mantrapurohitāḥ tataḥ senāpatiḥ paścāt praśāstā ca niṣedatuḥ
english: All the counsellors and the priest sat in order of precedence; then the general and the overseer sat down after them.

sanskrit: tatas tatra muhūrtena nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ upātiṣṭhanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanat
english: Then in a moment, by the command of Bharadvāja, rivers of rice-pudding came and presented themselves before Bharata.

sanskrit: tāsām ubhayataḥ kūlaṃ pāṇḍumṛttikalepanāḥ ramyāś cāvasathā divyā brahmaṇas tu prasādajāḥ
english: On both banks of those rivers, smeared with white clay, stood pleasant and divine rest-houses, born of the grace of the brahman sage.

sanskrit: tenaiva ca muhūrtena divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ āgur viṃśatisāhasrā brahmaṇā prahitāḥ striyaḥ
english: And in that very moment, twenty thousand women adorned with divine ornaments came, sent by Brahmā.

sanskrit: suvarṇamaṇimuktena pravālena ca śobhitāḥ āgur viṃśatisāhasrāḥ kuberaprahitāḥ striyaḥ
english: Twenty thousand women, resplendent with gold, gems, pearls, and coral, came, sent by Kubera.

sanskrit: yābhir gṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate āgur viṃśatisāhasrā nandanād apsarogaṇāḥ
english: Twenty thousand apsarases came from Nandana — those by whose touch a man appears as if beside himself with rapture.

sanskrit: nāradas tumburur gopaḥ parvataḥ sūryavarcasaḥ ete gandharvarājāno bharatasyāgrato jaguḥ
english: Nārada, Tumburu, Gopa, Parvata, and Sūryavarcas — these kings of the gandharvas sang before Bharata.

sanskrit: alambusā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkātha vāmanā upānṛtyaṃs tu bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt
english: Alambusā, Miśrakeśī, Puṇḍarīkā, and Vāmanā danced before Bharata by the command of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: yāni mālyāni deveṣu yāni caitrarathe vane prayāge tāny adṛśyanta bharadvājasya śāsanāt
english: The garlands that exist among the gods and in the Caitraratha forest were seen at Prayāga by the command of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: bilvā mārdaṅgikā āsañ śamyā grāhā bibhītakāḥ aśvatthā nartakāś cāsan bharadvājasya tejasā
english: By the power of Bharadvāja, bilva trees became mṛdaṅga drummers, śamī trees became players of the time-beaters, bibhītaka trees became players of stringed instruments, and aśvattha trees became dancers.

sanskrit: tataḥ saralatālāś ca tilakā naktamālakāḥ prahṛṣṭās tatra saṃpetuḥ kubjābhūtātha vāmanāḥ
english: Then sarala, tāla, tilaka, and naktamāla trees, filled with delight, rushed together there, having become hunchbacks and dwarfs.

sanskrit: śiṃśapāmalakī jambūr yāś cānyāḥ kānane latāḥ pramadā vigrahaṃ kṛtvā bharadvājāśrame 'vasan
english: Śiṃśapā, āmalakī, jambū, and the other creepers of the forest, having assumed the forms of beautiful women, dwelt in the hermitage of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: surāṃ surāpāḥ pibata pāyasaṃ ca bubhukśitāḥ māṃsani ca sumedhyāni bhakṣyantāṃ yāvad icchatha
english: "Let those who drink wine drink surā! Let the hungry eat rice-pudding! And let them eat the finest meats to their heart's desire!"

sanskrit: utsādya snāpayanti sma nadītīreṣu valguṣu apy ekam ekaṃ puruṣaṃ pramadāḥ satpa cāṣṭa ca
english: On the beautiful riverbanks, groups of seven and eight women bathed and anointed each man, one by one.

sanskrit: saṃvahantyaḥ samāpetur nāryo ruciralocanāḥ parimṛjya tathānyonyaṃ pāyayanti varāṅganāḥ
english: The women with lovely eyes rushed forward, massaging and wiping each other, and those beautiful women plied the men with drink.

sanskrit: hayān gajān kharān uṣṭrāṃs tathaiva surabheḥ sutān ikṣūṃś ca madhujālāṃś ca bhojayanti sma vāhanān ikṣvākuvarayodhānāṃ codayanto mahābalāḥ
english: They fed the horses, elephants, donkeys, camels, and the offspring of Surabhī with sugarcane and sweet treacle; and the mighty warriors of the Ikṣvāku line urged on their mounts.

sanskrit: nāśvabandho 'śvam ājānān na gajaṃ kuñjaragrahaḥ mattapramattamuditā camūḥ sā tatra saṃbabhau
english: No horse-keeper knew his own horse; no elephant-driver knew his elephant. That army appeared there intoxicated, heedless, and merry.

sanskrit: tarpitā sarvakāmais te raktacandanarūṣitāḥ apsarogaṇasaṃyuktāḥ sainyā vācam udairayan
english: Satisfied with all their desires, smeared with red sandalwood, and attended by the throngs of apsarases, the soldiers cried out:

sanskrit: naivāyodhyāṃ gamiṣyāmo na gamiṣyāma daṇḍakān kuśalaṃ bharatasyāstu rāmasyāstu tathā sukham
english: "We will not go back to Ayodhyā! Nor will we go to the Daṇḍaka forest! May Bharata fare well! And may Rāma find happiness!"

sanskrit: iti pādātayodhāś ca hastyaśvārohabandhakāḥ anāthās taṃ vidhiṃ labdhvā vācam etām udairayan
english: Thus the infantry soldiers, the elephant-riders, horsemen, and grooms — otherwise without a lord — on receiving that bounty, uttered these words.

sanskrit: saṃprahṛṣṭā vinedus te narās tatra sahasraśaḥ bharatasyānuyātāraḥ svarge 'yam iti cābruvan
english: Those thousands of men who had followed Bharata shouted with great joy and said, "This is heaven itself!"

sanskrit: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāṃ tad annam amṛtopamam divyān udvīkṣya bhakṣyāṃs tān abhavad bhakṣaṇe matiḥ
english: Even after they had eaten their fill of that food equal to nectar, on seeing those divine delicacies they felt the desire to eat again.

sanskrit: preṣyāś ceṭyaś ca vadhvaś ca balasthāś cāpi sarvaśaḥ babhūvus te bhṛśaṃ tṛptāḥ sarve cāhatavāsasaḥ
english: The servants, slave-girls, young wives, and all the fighting men were exceedingly satisfied, and all were clad in fresh garments.

sanskrit: kuñjarāś ca kharoṣṭraś ca go'śvāś ca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ babhūvuḥ subhṛtās tatra nānyo hy anyam akalpayat
english: The elephants, donkeys, camels, cows, horses, deer, and birds were all well-fed there; and no one tended to another's animal by mistake.

sanskrit: nāśuklavāsās tatrāsīt kṣudhito malino 'pi vā rajasā dhvastakeśo vā naraḥ kaś cid adṛśyata
english: Not a single man was seen there without white garments, nor hungry, nor dirty, nor with hair dishevelled with dust.

sanskrit: ājaiś cāpi ca vārāhair niṣṭhānavarasaṃcayaiḥ phalaniryūhasaṃsiddhaiḥ sūpair gandharasānvitaiḥ
english: And with goat and boar meats cooked to perfection, with soups prepared with the essence of fruits, fragrant and savoury,

sanskrit: puṣpadhvajavatīḥ pūrṇāḥ śuklasyānnasya cābhitaḥ dadṛśur vismitās tatra narā lauhīḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: bearing flower-banners, filled all around with white food — thousands of iron vessels were seen there with amazement by the men.

sanskrit: babhūvur vanapārśveṣu kūpāḥ pāyasakardamāḥ tāś ca kāmadughā gāvo drumāś cāsan madhuścyutaḥ
english: On the outskirts of the forest there appeared wells of rice-pudding, wish-fulfilling cows, and trees dripping with honey.

sanskrit: vāpyo maireyapūrṇāś ca mṛṣṭamāṃsacayair vṛtāḥ prataptapiṭharaiś cāpi mārgamāyūrakaukkuṭaiḥ
english: Tanks were filled with maireya wine, surrounded by heaps of choice meat, and with roasting-pans of roadside peacock and chicken.

sanskrit: pātrīṇāṃ ca sahasrāṇi śātakumbhamayāni ca sthālyaḥ kumbhyaḥ karambhyaś ca dadhipūrṇāḥ susaṃskṛtāḥ yauvanasthasya gaurasya kapitthasya sugandhinaḥ
english: Thousands of golden vessels appeared, along with cooking-pots, jars, and barley-gruel bowls filled with well-prepared curds, of the fragrant white kapittha fruit in its prime.

sanskrit: hradāḥ pūrṇā rasālasya dadhnaḥ śvetasya cāpare babhūvuḥ pāyasasyānte śarkarāyāś ca saṃcayāḥ
english: Some lakes were filled with sweet mango juice, others with white curds; and at the end appeared heaps of rice-pudding and piles of sugar.

sanskrit: kalkāṃś cūrṇakaṣāyāṃś ca snānāni vividhāni ca dadṛśur bhājanasthāni tīrtheṣu saritāṃ narāḥ
english: At the bathing-ghats of the rivers, the men saw various unguents, powders, astringent preparations, and bathing requisites stored in vessels.

sanskrit: śuklān aṃśumataś cāpi dantadhāvanasaṃcayān śuklāṃś candanakalkāṃś ca samudgeṣv avatiṣṭhataḥ
english: Bright, fresh tooth-cleaning twigs in heaps, and white sandal-wood pastes stood in their containers.

sanskrit: darpaṇān parimṛṣṭāṃś ca vāsasāṃ cāpi saṃcayān pādukopānahāṃ caiva yugmān yatra sahasraśaḥ
english: There too were polished mirrors, heaps of garments, and thousands of pairs of wooden sandals and shoes.

sanskrit: āñjanīḥ kaṅkatān kūrcāṃś chatrāṇi ca dhanūṃṣi ca marmatrāṇāni citrāṇi śayanāny āsanāni ca
english: Collyrium applicators, combs, brushes, parasols, bows, varied pieces of armour, couches, and seats as well.

sanskrit: pratipānahradān pūrṇān kharoṣṭragajavājinām avagāhya sutīrthāṃś ca hradān sotpala puṣkarān
english: Watering-ponds filled for donkeys, camels, elephants, and horses; and beautiful pools to bathe in, adorned with blue lotuses and water-lilies.

sanskrit: nīlavaidūryavarṇāṃś ca mṛdūn yavasasaṃcayān nirvāpārthaṃ paśūnāṃ te dadṛśus tatra sarvaśaḥ
english: And soft heaps of barley, the colour of blue vaidūrya gems, for the feeding of the animals — all these they saw there everywhere.

sanskrit: vyasmayanta manuṣyās te svapnakalpaṃ tad adbhutam dṛṣṭvātithyaṃ kṛtaṃ tādṛg bharatasya maharṣiṇā
english: Those men were struck with wonder at that marvellous scene, like unto a dream, on seeing the such hospitality rendered to Bharata by the great sage.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ ramamāṇānāṃ devānām iva nandane bharadvājāśrame ramye sā rātrir vyatyavartata
english: Thus, as they revelled as if in the Nandana grove of the gods, that night passed away in the lovely hermitage of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: pratijagmuś ca tā nadyo gandharvāś ca yathāgatam bharadvājam anujñāpya tāś ca sarvā varāṅganāḥ
english: Then those rivers, the gandharvas, and all those beautiful women departed in the way they had come, after taking leave of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tathaiva mattā madirotkaṭā narās tathaiva divyāgurucandanokṣitāḥ tathaiva divyā vividhāḥ sraguttamāḥ pṛthakprakīrṇā manujaiḥ pramarditāḥ
english: Just so those men remained intoxicated and stupefied with wine, sprinkled with divine aguru and sandalwood; just so those various divine and choice garlands lay scattered and trampled by men.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ rajanīm uṣya bharataḥ saparicchadaḥ kṛtātithyo bharadvājaṃ kāmād abhijagāma ha
english: Then Bharata, having spent that night with his retinue, having been thus hospitably treated, approached Bharadvāja of his own accord.

sanskrit: tam ṛṣiḥ puruṣavyāghraṃ prekṣya prāñjalim āgatam hutāgnihotro bharataṃ bharadvājo 'bhyabhāṣata
english: The sage Bharadvāja, having performed the agnihotra oblation, looked upon that tiger among men as he came with joined palms and addressed Bharata.

sanskrit: kaccid atra sukhā rātris tavāsmadviṣaye gatā samagras te janaḥ kaccid ātithye śaṃsa me 'nagha
english: "Did you pass a comfortable night here in our domain? Is your whole company complete? Tell me, O sinless one, how was the hospitality?"

sanskrit: tam uvācāñjaliṃ kṛtvā bharato 'bhipraṇamya ca āśramād abhiniṣkrantam ṛṣim uttama tejasaṃ
english: Bharata, having joined his palms and bowed down, spoke to the sage of supreme splendour who had come forth from the hermitage.

sanskrit: sukhoṣito 'smi bhagavan samagrabalavāhanaḥ tarpitaḥ sarvakāmaiḥ sāmātyo balavat tvayā
english: "I have spent the night in comfort, revered sir, with my entire force and cavalry. I and my ministers have been powerfully satisfied with all our desires by you.

sanskrit: apetaklamasaṃtāpāḥ subhakṣyāḥ supratiśrayāḥ api preṣyān upādāya sarve sma susukhoṣitāḥ
english: Free from fatigue and distress, provided with excellent food and excellent lodgings, all of us — including even the servants — have slept in great comfort.

sanskrit: āmantraye 'haṃ bhagavan kāmaṃ tvām ṛṣisattama samīpaṃ prasthitaṃ bhrātur maireṇekṣasva cakṣuṣā
english: I take leave of you, revered sir, O best of seers, as I set out towards my brother's presence — look upon me with a kindly eye.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ tasya dharmajña dhārmikasya mahātmanaḥ ācakṣva katamo mārgaḥ kiyān iti ca śaṃsa me
english: Tell me, O knower of dharma, the hermitage of that righteous great-souled one — which is the path, and how far is it? Tell me."

sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭas tu bharataṃ bhrātṛdarśanalālasaṃ pratyuvāca mahātejā bharadvājo mahātapāḥ
english: Thus questioned, the greatly brilliant and greatly ascetic Bharadvāja replied to Bharata, who was eager to behold his brother.

sanskrit: bharatārdhatṛtīyeṣu yojaneṣv ajane vane citrakūṭo giris tatra ramyanirdarakānanaḥ
english: "O Bharata, at two and a half yojanas from here, in the uninhabited forest, is Mount Citrakūṭa, pleasant with its caves and groves.

sanskrit: uttaraṃ pārśvam āsādya tasya mandākinī nadī puṣpitadrumasaṃchannā ramyapuṣpitakānanā
english: On its northern side flows the river Mandākinī, overhung with flowering trees, with beautiful and flowering groves.

sanskrit: anantaraṃ tat saritaś citrakūṭaś ca parvataḥ tato parṇakuṭī tāta tatra tau vasato dhruvam
english: Adjacent to that river is Mount Citrakūṭa, and beyond it is the leaf-hut — there, dear one, those two certainly dwell.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇenaiva mārgeṇa savyadakṣiṇam eva ca gajavājirathākīrṇāṃ vāhinīṃ vāhinīpate vāhayasva mahābhāga tato drakṣyasi rāghavam
english: Lead your army, filled with elephants, horses, and chariots, by the southern path, keeping it to your left and right, O commander of forces, O fortunate one — then you will see Rāghava."

sanskrit: prayāṇam iti ca śrutvā rājarājasya yoṣitaḥ hitvā yānāni yānārhā brāhmaṇaṃ paryavārayan
english: On hearing of the departure of that king of kings, the women — those who were worthy of conveyances — left their vehicles and gathered around the brahman sage.

sanskrit: vepamānā kṛśā dīnā saha devyā sumantriyā kausalyā tatra jagrāha karābhyāṃ caraṇau muneḥ
english: Trembling, thin, and wretched, Kausalyā, together with the queens and Sumantrī, clasped the feet of the sage with both hands.

sanskrit: asamṛddhena kāmena sarvalokasya garhitā kaikeyī tasya jagrāha caraṇau savyapatrapā
english: Kaikeyī, whose desire was unfulfilled, condemned by all the world, grasped his feet with shame.

sanskrit: taṃ pradakṣiṇam āgamya bhagavantaṃ mahāmunim adūrād bharatasyaiva tasthau dīnamanās tadā
english: Having circumambulated that blessed great sage, she stood at a little distance near Bharata himself, dejected in mind.

sanskrit: tataḥ papraccha bharataṃ bharadvājo dṛḍhavrataḥ viśeṣaṃ jñātum icchāmi mātṝṇāṃ tava rāghava
english: Then Bharadvāja of firm vows asked Bharata: "I wish to know in detail about your mothers, O Rāghava."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bharato bharadvājena dhārmikaḥ uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā vākyaṃ vacanakovidaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Bharadvāja, the righteous Bharata, skilled in speech, with joined palms, spoke these words.

sanskrit: yām imāṃ bhagavan dīnāṃ śokān aśanakarśitām pitur hi mahiṣīṃ devīṃ devatām iva paśyasi
english: "She whom you see, revered sir — wretched, emaciated by grief and scanty food — she is the chief queen of my father, worshipful as a goddess.

sanskrit: eṣā taṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ siṃhavikrāntagāminam kausalyā suṣuve rāmaṃ dhātāram aditir yathā
english: This is Kausalyā, who bore Rāma, that tiger among men who walks with a lion's gait — as Aditi bore the Sustainer Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: asyā vāmabhujaṃ śliṣṭā yaiṣā tiṣṭhati durmanāḥ karṇikārasya śākheva śīrṇapuṣpā vanāntare
english: She who clings to her left arm and stands there heavy-hearted, like a branch of the karṇikāra with withered flowers in the heart of the forest —

sanskrit: etasyās tau sutau devyāḥ kumārau devavarṇinau ubhau lakṣmaṇaśatrughnau vīrau satyaparākramau
english: her two sons, O queen, are the princes of divine appearance — both Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, heroes of true valour.

sanskrit: yasyāḥ kṛte naravyāghrau jīvanāśam ito gatau rājā putravihīnaś ca svargaṃ daśaratho gataḥ
english: On account of whom those two tigers among men departed from here losing their life in the forest, and the king Daśaratha, bereft of his son, departed to heaven —

sanskrit: aiśvaryakāmāṃ kaikeyīm anāryām āryarūpiṇīm mamaitāṃ mātaraṃ viddhi nṛśaṃsāṃ pāpaniścayām yatomūlaṃ hi paśyāmi vyasanaṃ mahad ātmanaḥ
english: know that this woman — Kaikeyī, craving for power, ignoble though bearing a noble form, cruel and fixed in sin — is my mother, from whom I see springing all this great calamity upon myself."

sanskrit: ity uktvā naraśārdūlo bāṣpagadgadayā girā sa niśaśvāsa tāmrākṣo kruddho nāga ivāsakṛt
english: Having said this, that tiger among men, with a voice choked with tears, his eyes red, sighed repeatedly like an angry serpent.

sanskrit: bharadvājo maharṣis taṃ bruvantaṃ bharataṃ tadā pratyuvāca mahābuddhir idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Then the great sage Bharadvāja, of great wisdom, replied to Bharata as he spoke thus, with these meaningful words.

sanskrit: na doṣeṇāvagantavyā kaikeyī bharata tvayā rāmapravrājanaṃ hy etat sukhodarkaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Kaikeyī must not be regarded as guilty by you, O Bharata — for this exile of Rāma will prove to be productive of happiness in the end.

sanskrit: abhivādya tu saṃsiddhaḥ kṛtvā cainaṃ pradakṣiṇam āmantrya bharataḥ sainyaṃ yujyatām ity acodayat
english: Having bowed to him, having circumambulated him, and taken his leave, Bharata, his purpose fulfilled, urged the army: "Let the army be made ready!"

sanskrit: tato vājirathān yuktvā divyān hemapariṣkritān adhyārohat prayāṇārthī bahūn bahuvidho janaḥ
english: Then, having yoked the divine horses to the chariots adorned with gold, men of many kinds mounted them in great numbers, ready for the march.

sanskrit: gajakanyāgajāś caiva hemakakṣyāḥ patākinaḥ jīmūtā iva gharmānte saghoṣāḥ saṃpratasthire
english: Young she-elephants and bull-elephants, with golden girths, bearing banners, set out trumpeting like rain-clouds at the end of summer.

sanskrit: vividhāny api yānāni mahāni ca laghūni ca prayayuḥ sumahārhāṇi pādair eva padātayaḥ
english: Varied vehicles, both large and small, of great worth, moved forward; and the infantry marched on foot.

sanskrit: atha yānapravekais tu kausalyāpramukhāḥ striyaḥ rāmadarśanakāṅkṣiṇyaḥ prayayur muditās tadā
english: Then the women with Kausalyā at their head, eager to behold Rāma, proceeded joyfully in the finest vehicles.

sanskrit: sa cārkataruṇābhāsāṃ niyuktāṃ śibikāṃ śubhām āsthāya prayayau śrīmān bharataḥ saparicchadaḥ
english: And the splendid Bharata, with his retinue, mounted a beautiful palanquin harnessed and gleaming like the young sun, and set forth.

sanskrit: sā prayātā mahāsenā gajavājirathākulā dakṣiṇāṃ diśam āvṛtya mahāmegha ivotthitaḥ vanāni tu vyatikramya juṣṭāni mṛgapakṣibhiḥ
english: That great army, teeming with elephants, horses, and chariots, having set out and turned toward the southern direction, rising like a great cloud, crossed through forests frequented by deer and birds.

sanskrit: sā saṃprahṛṣṭadvipavājiyodhā vitrāsayantī mṛgapakṣisaṃghān mahad vanaṃ tat pravigāhamānā rarāja senā bharatasya tatra
english: That army of Bharata, with its rejoicing elephants, horses, and warriors, frightening the herds of deer and flocks of birds, as it plunged into that great forest, shone magnificently there.

sanskrit: tayā mahatyā yāyinyā dhvajinyā vanavāsinaḥ arditā yūthapā mattāḥ sayūthāḥ saṃpradudruvuḥ
english: Harassed by that great and advancing army with its banners, the leaders of elephant herds, maddened, fled away together with their herds.

sanskrit: ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṃghāś ca ruravaś ca samantataḥ dṛśyante vanarājīṣu giriṣv api nadīṣu ca
english: Bears, herds of spotted deer, and ruruantelopes were seen on all sides in the forest glades, on the mountains, and near the rivers.

sanskrit: sa saṃpratasthe dharmātmā prīto daśarathātmajaḥ vṛto mahatyā nādinyā senayā caturaṅgayā
english: That righteous son of Daśaratha set out with gladness, surrounded by the great, tumultuous, four-divisioned army.

sanskrit: sāgaraughanibhā senā bharatasya mahātmanaḥ mahīṃ saṃchādayām āsa prāvṛṣi dyām ivāmbudaḥ
english: The army of the great-souled Bharata, resembling the flood of the ocean, covered the earth as clouds cover the sky in the rainy season.

sanskrit: turaṃgaughair avatatā vāraṇaiś ca mahājavaiḥ anālakṣyā ciraṃ kālaṃ tasmin kāle babhūva bhūḥ
english: Covered by the multitudes of horses and by swift-moving elephants, the earth was invisible for a long time during that period.

sanskrit: sa yātvā dūram adhvānaṃ supariśrānta vāhanaḥ uvāca bharataḥ śrīmān vasiṣṭhaṃ mantriṇāṃ varam
english: Having travelled a great distance, with his mounts greatly tired, the splendid Bharata spoke to Vasiṣṭha, the best of counsellors.

sanskrit: yādṛśaṃ lakṣyate rūpaṃ yathā caiva śrutaṃ mayā vyaktaṃ prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yam abravīt
english: "The landscape that appears to the eye and what I have heard described — evidently we have arrived at the region that Bharadvāja indicated.

sanskrit: ayaṃ giriś citrakūṭas tathā mandākinī nadī etat prakāśate dūrān nīlameghanibhaṃ vanam
english: This is Mount Citrakūṭa, and there the river Mandākinī; and that forest visible from afar, resembling a dark cloud, gleams before us.

sanskrit: gireḥ sānūni ramyāṇi citrakūṭasya saṃprati vāraṇair avamṛdyante māmakaiḥ parvatopamaiḥ
english: The pleasant ridges of Mount Citrakūṭa are now being trampled by my elephants, which are themselves like mountains.

sanskrit: muñcanti kusumāny ete nagāḥ parvatasānuṣu nīlā ivātapāpāye toyaṃ toyadharā ghanāḥ
english: These trees on the mountain ridges are shedding their flowers like dark rain-clouds releasing water at the end of summer heat.

sanskrit: kinnarācaritoddeśaṃ paśya śatrughna parvatam hayaiḥ samantād ākīrṇaṃ makarair iva sāgaram
english: Look, O Śatrughna, at this mountain haunted by kinnaras, covered all around by horses — like the ocean filled with sea-monsters.

sanskrit: ete mṛgagaṇā bhānti śīghravegāḥ pracoditāḥ vāyupraviddhāḥ śaradi megharājya ivāmbare
english: These herds of deer, driven forward at swift speed, scatter in every direction like clouds tossed by the wind in the sky in autumn.

sanskrit: kurvanti kusumāpīḍāñ śiraḥsu surabhīn amī meghaprakāśaiḥ phalakair dākṣiṇātyā yathā narāḥ
english: These trees place fragrant flower-crowns on their crests with their cloud-gleaming canopies, like the men of the south with their garlands.

sanskrit: niṣkūjam iva bhūtvedaṃ vanaṃ ghorapradarśanam ayodhyeva janākīrṇā saṃprati pratibhāti mā
english: This forest, though it once appeared fierce and silent, now seems to me like Ayodhyā thronged with people.

sanskrit: khurair udīrito reṇur divaṃ pracchādya tiṣṭhati taṃ vahaty anilaḥ śīghraṃ kurvann iva mama priyam
english: The dust raised by hooves stands covering the sky; the wind carries it swiftly, as if doing me a favour.

sanskrit: syandanāṃs turagopetān sūtamukhyair adhiṣṭhitān etān saṃpatataḥ śīghraṃ paśya śatrughna kānane
english: Look, O Śatrughna, at these chariots yoked with horses, manned by chief charioteers, rushing swiftly through the forest.

sanskrit: etān vitrāsitān paśya barhiṇaḥ priyadarśanān etam āviśataḥ śailam adhivāsaṃ patatriṇām
english: Look at these lovely peacocks, frightened by the commotion, entering this mountain that is the abode of birds.

sanskrit: atimātram ayaṃ deśo manojñaḥ pratibhāti mā tāpasānāṃ nivāso 'yaṃ vyaktaṃ svargapatho yathā
english: This region appears to me exceedingly beautiful; this abode of ascetics clearly appears like the path to heaven.

sanskrit: mṛgā mṛgībhiḥ sahitā bahavaḥ pṛṣatā vane manojña rūpā lakṣyante kusumair iva citritāḥ
english: Many deer together with does, and spotted antelopes in the forest, of pleasing form, are seen like paintings adorned with flowers.

sanskrit: sādhu sainyāḥ pratiṣṭhantāṃ vicinvantu ca kānanam yathā tau puruṣavyāghrau dṛśyete rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: "Let the soldiers halt and search the forest, so that those two tigers among men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, may be seen."

sanskrit: bharatasya vacaḥ śrutvā puruṣāḥ śastrapāṇayaḥ viviśus tad vanaṃ śūrā dhūmaṃ ca dadṛśus tataḥ
english: Hearing Bharata's words, armed men, heroes all, entered that forest, and there they saw smoke.

sanskrit: te samālokya dhūmāgram ūcur bharatam āgatāḥ nāmanuṣye bhavaty agnir vyaktam atraiva rāghavau
english: Observing the tip of the smoke, they came back and said to Bharata: "Fire does not exist in an uninhabited place — evidently the Rāghavas are right here."

sanskrit: atha nātra naravyāghrau rājaputrau paraṃtapau anye rāmopamāḥ santi vyaktam atra tapasvinaḥ
english: "Or, if those two tiger-princes, scorchers of foes, are not here, then there are clearly other ascetics dwelling here who are like Rāma."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā bharatas teṣāṃ vacanaṃ sādhu saṃmatam sainyān uvāca sarvāṃs tān amitrabalamardanaḥ
english: Hearing that well-considered speech of theirs, Bharata, crusher of the power of enemies, addressed all those soldiers.

sanskrit: yat tā bhavantas tiṣṭhantu neto gantavyam agrataḥ aham eva gamiṣyāmi sumantro gurur eva ca
english: "Let all of you halt here — no one is to go ahead. I alone shall go forward, and Sumantra, and the preceptor as well."

sanskrit: evam uktās tataḥ sarve tatra tasthuḥ samantataḥ bharato yatra dhūmāgraṃ tatra dṛṣṭiṃ samādadhat
english: Thus instructed, all of them halted there on every side, while Bharata fixed his gaze on the place where the tip of the smoke arose.

sanskrit: vyavasthitā yā bharatena sā camūr nirīkṣamāṇāpi ca dhūmam agrataḥ babhūva hṛṣṭā nacireṇa jānatī priyasya rāmasya samāgamaṃ tadā
english: That army which had been halted by Bharata, even as it looked toward the tip of the smoke ahead, before long became joyful, knowing that the meeting with beloved Rāma was at hand.
